articles.title: 🕵️ A.I. Company Catches A Foreign Influence Op Using Its Chatbot; Propaganda Now Comes With A Word Count And A Tone Setting
articles.dateline: SAN FRANCISCO — reported through a freshly closed loophole
paras: An AI lab announced it shut down a covert foreign influence operation that had been using its chatbot to churn out propaganda — confirming that the timeless craft of manufacturing lies has been thoroughly disrupted by a startup, and now ships with autocomplete.

"We're committed to preventing abuse," the company said, of a service so useful that even the disinformation industry adopted it to boost productivity. Analysts note the propagandist's job has evolved from "write a thousand fake comments" to "ask nicely and click regenerate," which is grim, efficient, and depressingly on-trend.

articles.title: 🖥️ Apple Ships A Tiny Box That Runs A.I. On Your Desk; The Cloud Is Now Slightly Closer To Home
articles.dateline: CUPERTINO — reported from a very small, very warm cube
paras: Apple quietly released a new Mac mini built for the on-device AI era, letting the machine think for itself without shipping your every thought off to a distant data center — a refreshing idea in which your computer keeps its opinions, and your secrets, indoors.

"It's powerful and private," Apple said, of a little box that runs models locally and, mercifully, does not first email them to a warehouse in another state. Reviewers praised the privacy while noting the device runs warm enough to double as a hand-warmer, a space heater, and, on cold mornings, a genuine reason to sit closer to your desk.

articles.title: ⚡ New Chip Makes A.I. Agents 'Instantaneous'; They Now Finish The Task Before You've Explained It
articles.dateline: SANTA CLARA — reported faster than you can read this
paras: The dominant chipmaker pushed specialized inference silicon into full production to make AI agents feel instantaneous — so responsive that the assistant now completes your request in the brief silence between you deciding to speak and actually speaking.

"Latency is the enemy," engineers explained, of hardware built so agents never make you wait, forever eliminating the last human buffer against a machine that acts before you've finished your sentence. Early users report it is thrilling, seamless, and only occasionally unsettling to be helped before asking, like a butler who has read the future and finds it a little dull.

articles.title: 🔬 Phone Maker Debuts Its Own 3-Nanometer Chip; Everybody Now Makes Their Own Silicon, Like Sourdough In 2020
articles.dateline: BEIJING — reported through a microscope, again
paras: A major phone maker showed off its latest homegrown 3-nanometer chip, joining the ever-growing club of companies that decided the only way to stop depending on someone else's silicon was to painstakingly bake their own.

"Self-reliance is the goal," the company said, of an industry-wide urge to control its own chips that carries all the collective energy of everyone starting a sourdough during a lockdown. Analysts note that in 2026, announcing you make your own silicon is less a technical milestone than a personality — and everyone has it.

articles.title: 🔌 Hottest A.I. Startup Of The Week Makes... Power Supplies; Even The Boring Parts Are Now A Gold Mine
articles.dateline: MUNICH-ISH — filed from beside a very in-demand transformer
paras: A chip company is acquiring a startup that develops digital power technology for AI data centers, proving the AI boom has grown so vast that even the deeply unglamorous business of "making sure the electricity arrives correctly" is now a multimillion-dollar prize.

"Power efficiency is critical," executives said, of the once-invisible plumbing that has quietly become the industry's most coveted skill. Analysts note the surest sign of a bubble — or a genuine revolution — is when the least exciting job in the building suddenly gets a standing ovation and a buyout offer.

horoscopes.text: Something will help you before you even ask today. Enjoy it. Also, perhaps, be a little concerned.
You will consider making your own chip today. Or bread. The urge is identical. Follow it wherever it leads.
Mercury runs locally now, on your desk, warm to the touch. Keep your secrets close and your vents clear.

tech_tip: If your new computer runs A.I. 'on device,' that's good for privacy — and great for warming your hands. Every feature is two features if you're cold enough.
gadget_watch: Apple's new Mac mini keeps your A.I. (and your thoughts) at home, and it runs warm enough to notice. Meanwhile chips are now so fast your assistant answers before you ask — a butler from the future, mildly bored.
